setting.note: Swift's satire sends its narrator to invented islands, but it frames every voyage in a real, ordinary England: a ship's surgeon from Nottinghamshire who trains and settles around the London docks and sails from English ports before the fantastical lands begin.

rights.originalWork: First published anonymously in 1726 by Jonathan Swift; long out of copyright. Mapped as a cited work: no text stored, no passages reproduced. The places are facts and the notes are our own.
rights.textSource: None stored. A cited book reproduces no text.
rights.territoryNotes: Locations and original commentary only. No reproduction of any text, in any territory.
rights.attribution: Gulliver's Travels, Jonathan Swift (1726). Locations mapped by Read the Places; the fantastical islands are satirical inventions and are not mapped.

palette.note: The green of the English shore the voyages keep returning to. A cited book's colour is not a quotation; it still has to be legible, and this clears WCAG AA on paper.
